findings.problem: This `simp↓` lemma is stated for a general `b`, so it also fires on the literal `b = false`. The `false` basis vector is the unit, and the canonical simp rules for the unit are `symmetricThreeCharThreeSimpleClassBasis_false` (also `simp↓`) and `resK0_one` (`@[simp]`). Pre-lemmas fire at the outer term first, so `resK0 k _ (symmetricThreeCharThreeSimpleClassBasis k false)` should be rewritten by this lemma before the argument is visited. The result is `symmetricThreeStabilizerSimpleClassBasis k a false`. No stabilizer analogue of `_false` appears in Stabilizer.lean, so the simp-set `symmetricThreeStabilizerSimpleClassBasis_apply` should then expand this to `ExactK0.of (FGModuleCat.of … (ofLinearCharacter 1).asModule)`, not `1`. Meanwhile `resK0 k _ 1` should simplify to `1` by `resK0_one`. The two spellings of the same element would therefore get different normal forms, and the rule set looks non-confluent on the trivial class. The same lemma is also what stops `Module.Basis.repr_self` from applying afterwards, because the `_apply` rule expands the basis vector first.
findings.proposed_change: Add a companion lemma in Stabilizer.lean, `symmetricThreeStabilizerSimpleClassBasis_false : symmetricThreeStabilizerSimpleClassBasis k a false = 1`, as `@[simp↓]`. It would mirror `symmetricThreeCharThreeSimpleClassBasis_false`. Alternatively, restrict the restriction lemma in this file to `true`, with a separate `false` case stated as `resK0 … (basis k false) = 1`. A `simp↓` rule of that kind, or the composite `_false` rule plus `resK0_one`, would make both spellings of the unit reach `1`.
findings.benefit: `simp` would send `resK0` of the trivial class to `1` however it is written, and the trivial class would have one normal form on both S₃ and the stabilizer. Users would no longer get a stray `ExactK0.of (… asModule)` term for the trivial line after restriction. The rule set would also match the existing `_false` convention in Simple.lean.
